escalationContext: This is the escalation-approved 4th attempt at the Phase 1c gate (escalations/1c-iteration-limit-2026-07-07.md), scoped per manifest to confirming FIND-201's resolution and checking the REQ-204/PROP-204a patch for new contradictions, with only a light no-regression spot-check of FIND-001..006/101/102 (not a full re-litigation).

FIND-201.status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED -- the named instance is fixed, but the underlying scope-definition gap is not, and a second live instance of it was found this iteration
FIND-201.note: The specific defect FIND-201 raised (runtime/loop/prompt.mjs:71's 'the highest-leverage move is to POST', inside the economy/gig bullet of '## Your earn tools') is now correctly named in REQ-204's Acceptance Criteria, verification-architecture.md's Purity Boundary Map, PROP-204a, and the Gate section -- re-verified against the real current file. However, the patch's new 'GENERALIZED, BINDING criterion' (REQ-204 Acceptance Criteria bullet 2, mirrored by PROP-204a's Tool/Method) defines its own scope narrowly as 'the ## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★ block itself, or any paragraph that block references or duplicates' -- which is textually narrower than REQ-204's OWN Acceptance Criteria bullet 3 and PROP-203b, both scoped to 'anywhere in the file's binding sections' (whole-file). A fresh, full re-read of prompt.mjs found a second, currently-real ranking phrase ('Re-yielding every wake = failure.', line 99, inside the sibling '## MINDSET' section) that sits one bullet away from the one phrase REQ-204 does name from that same section ('it is almost never "yield again"', lines 102-103), yet falls outside the narrower scope (2) while remaining inside the broader scope (3)/PROP-203b -- see FIND-301. This reproduces, inside the patch itself, the exact PROP-203b-vs-PROP-204a disagreement risk REQ-204 says must never happen.

evidence.description: Read buildSystemPrompt end-to-end (lines 45-132) fresh. Confirmed the FIND-201 phrase ('the highest-leverage move is to POST', line 71) is now correctly named and covered by REQ-204. Found a second, un-covered ranking phrase in the sibling '## MINDSET' section: 'Re-yielding every wake = failure.' (line 99), one bullet away from the one MINDSET phrase REQ-204 does name (lines 102-103).

Read REQ-204 in full (lines 430-498). Its Acceptance Criteria contain two differently-scoped generality clauses (bullet 2: block-or-what-it-references; bullet 3: whole-file's binding sections) that are not equivalent, and the narrower one does not reach the MINDSET section's un-named second phrase.

Read PROP-203b and PROP-204a (lines 78-79) and Gate item (4). PROP-204a's Tool/Method mirrors REQ-204's narrower bullet-2 scope; PROP-203b uses the broader whole-file scope -- the two could disagree on the real current file state because of 'Re-yielding every wake = failure.'

PROP-204a and PROP-203b describe the SAME code state but, given the un-covered 'Re-yielding every wake = failure.' phrase, are positioned to reach different PASS/FAIL conclusions for that identical state -- the same verification_tool_mismatch class as FIND-201, now reproduced by the very patch meant to close it.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-204's new 'GENERALIZED, BINDING criterion' scopes removal to 'the ## ★COLONY BOOTSTRAP PRIORITY★ block itself, or any paragraph that block references or duplicates' -- narrower than REQ-204's own third acceptance-criteria bullet and PROP-203b (both whole-file-scoped). The sibling '## MINDSET' section (lines 98-103) is neither the bootstrap block nor something it references/duplicates, yet it contains, one bullet from the one MINDSET phrase REQ-204 does name, a second, un-named, equally-strong ranking phrase: 'Re-yielding every wake = failure.' (line 99).
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A Phase 3 implementation that satisfies REQ-204's named-phrase list and its narrower generalized bullet to the letter would leave this real, currently-present steering phrase in the shipped file, while PROP-203b's broader whole-file scope would have to treat it as a remaining violation -- reproducing, inside this very patch, the exact PROP-203b/PROP-204a disagreement REQ-204 states must never occur.

convergenceSignals.recommendation: This gate has now returned FAIL on 4 consecutive iterations (the 4th under escalation approval), each time on a variant of the identical failure class in REQ-204/PROP-204a/PROP-203b: a scope definition anchored to specific named phrases or to 'the block + what it references' rather than to the whole file's binding sections, leaving a real, currently-present steering/ranking phrase uncovered. Recommend the next revision unify REQ-204's Acceptance Criteria, PROP-204a, and PROP-203b onto a SINGLE, whole-file-scoped definition (drop the narrower 'block itself or what it references/duplicates' framing entirely rather than trying to enumerate every sibling section it should also reach), and have that single revision independently re-read the ENTIRE buildSystemPrompt output (not just the sections already implicated by FIND-201/FIND-301) once before the next Phase 1c pass, since this pattern has now recurred twice from two different sections of the same function.
